sources.label: Sources
sources.alerts: Alerts by the National Weather Service

hint.feelsLike: What the air feels like on skin. Wind strips heat away and humid air slows sweat from evaporating, so it can differ from the thermometer.
hint.humidity: Relative humidity: the water vapour in the air as a percentage of the most it can hold at this temperature. Warm air can hold more, so the same percentage means more moisture on a hot day.
hint.dewPoint: A temperature, not a percentage: cool the air to this point and its moisture condenses into dew. It measures the moisture actually in the air. From about 18 °C (65 °F) the air feels muggy.
hint.uv: The strength of the sun's skin-burning ultraviolet light right now, on the World Health Organization's scale; the week shows each day's peak. From 3 up, protection is advised. Thin cloud lets most of it through.
hint.pressure: The weight of the air above, adjusted to sea level so places at different heights compare. The average is about 1013 hPa (29.92 inHg); falling pressure often brings wind and rain.
hint.visibility: The farthest distance at which a large dark object can be seen against the sky. Below 1 km (0.6 mi) it counts as fog.
hint.pm25: Fine particles under 2.5 micrometres, from smoke and exhaust. Small enough to reach deep into the lungs.
hint.pm10: Particles under 10 micrometres: dust, pollen and mold spores.
hint.ozone: A gas sunlight makes from pollution. It irritates the airways, most on hot afternoons.
hint.no2: Nitrogen dioxide, mostly from traffic and burning fuel. It irritates the airways.
hint.wind: The sustained speed, and the direction the wind blows from: a south wind comes from the south.
hint.gusts: Short bursts above the sustained speed, lasting a few seconds. They are often strongest around showers and thunderstorms.
hint.rainfall: The depth of rain over the whole day. One millimetre is one litre of water on every square metre.
hint.cloudCover: The share of the sky covered by cloud. Clear nights cool faster, because cloud holds in the ground's heat.
hint.hours: The percentage is the chance of rain or snow falling here during that hour.
hint.aqi: The US index runs from 0 to 500 and follows whichever pollutant is worst. Up to 50 is good; above 100, sensitive groups should take care.

tiers.label: How sensitive data is treated
tiers.help: Every fact, entity and kind carries one tier, set once in the registry and enforced everywhere: storage, sync, export and the Gardener.

t0.name: Harmless
t0.text: Preferences and public facts: cuisines, recipes, stock, forecasts. The Gardener may read them when a tool declares them.

t1.name: Personal
t1.text: Ideas, notes, workouts, your home area, calendar events. Read the same way.

t2.name: Sensitive
t2.text: Allergies, body metrics, medical appointments, the home Place. The Gardener sees one only under a grant you give.

t3.name: Restricted
t3.text: Keys, tokens, identity documents, account numbers. Kept in the Vault or the keychain and never shown to a model.

egress.label: What left this device
egress.help: Every request Eden made in the last seven days, by where it went and the day. Bytes out count the request's address and body, not its headers; requests are counted apart. Apple's WeatherKit and the updater add their own traffic around what Eden hands them.
